sources.entry: AppPolice - App for macOS with a minimalistic UI which lets you quickly throttle down the CPU usage of any running process.

summary.one_liner: AppPolice is a minimalistic macOS app that lets you quickly throttle the CPU usage of any running process.
summary.what_it_does: AppPolice is a Mac OS X application with a minimalistic user interface. Its stated purpose is to let the user quickly throttle down the CPU usage of any running process. The README is short and gives no detail on how the throttling is implemented or what controls the UI offers. It states that the app requires OS X Lion 10.7 or later. Pre-built .dmg files are distributed through the repository's Releases page. Building from source requires cloning the ChromeMenu repository into the same directory, which provides a ChromeMenu.Framework dependency.
use_cases: slow down a CPU-hungry process on mac
reduce fan noise by limiting process CPU
keep a running program from hogging the processor
manage CPU usage of individual mac processes
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg file from the Releases page
Open the app on first run by right-clicking and choosing "Open" (needed once because the app is not opened normally by Gatekeeper)
To build from source: clone both AppPolice and ChromeMenu into the same directory
notable: Minimalistic macOS UI focused on one task: throttling CPU usage of running processes
Works on any running process, per the README
Distributed as a prebuilt .dmg via GitHub Releases
caveats: Requires OS X Lion 10.7 or later; macOS only
Building from source needs the separate ChromeMenu repository cloned alongside it
README is brief and does not describe the throttling method or document further features
